scope: Theorem B.1 (Polynomial-time obstruction from fixed-depth crossings) of the manuscript “Stretched-exponential barriers for typical SK initial states” (preprints/Stretched-exponential-barriers-for-typical-SK-initial-states-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 227 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7bc4d5a64b6465fe), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 55-56. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed β > 1 and every fixed a > 0, PJ, x0∼πJ { dJ (x0, na ) > 1 4 } −→ 1, (B.1) PJ, x0∼πJ { dJ disc(x0, ⌊na ⌋) > 1 4 } −→ 1. (B.2) 55 Consequently both P{TJ (x0) > na} and P{TJ disc(x0) > na} tend to one under the same joint law. Each assertion is equivalently a statement that the Gibbs mass of the indicated initial states tends to one in probability over J.
